Note::jaccard_tokens¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::jaccard_tokens(const Note& other) const

Word-Set Similarity Score Between Two Notes¶

jaccard_tokens(other) reduces each cell of self and the matching cell of other to a set of words and returns the Jaccard index of the two sets — the size of their intersection divided by the size of their union — as a shape-preserving Note of score strings. It is the word-level scoring member of the set-similarity family, alongside overlap_tokens (a containment score) and intersect_tokens (which returns the shared words themselves rather than a number).

How the score is computed¶

Each cell is tokenized with the ASCII word tokenizer (as tokenize_words does), lowercased, and deduplicated into a set A (from self) and B (from other). The score is

|A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B|

a value in [0, 1]: 1 when the two word sets are identical, 0 when they are disjoint. It is symmetric — a.jaccard_tokens(b) equals b.jaccard_tokens(a).

There is no length or stopword filter; for a score over content words only, use jaccard_terms.

Edge cases¶

  • Both sets empty (both cells tokenize to nothing) → "1.0": two empty sets are equal.

  • One set empty, the other not → "0.0".

Result shape and formatting¶

The result is a Note with the same shape as the pairing’s non-scalar side, one cell per comparison. Each score is formatted with up to six decimal places, trailing zeros trimmed, always at least one digit after the point: "1.0", "0.5", "0.666667". Parse with std::stod when you need a number.

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

Per cell and pairwise; equal numel or a scalar (numel() == 1) broadcast. Rejections raise pluss::Error:

  • either side in bytes mode → Note::jaccard_tokens requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes) (or rhs is bytes).

  • unequal numel with neither side a scalar → Note::jaccard_tokens expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

Example 1: Per-Cell Scores¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"the quick brown fox", "alpha beta gamma"})
        .jaccard_tokens(pluss::make_note({"the quick red fox", "beta gamma delta"})))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["0.6", "0.5"]

Cell 0: {the, quick, brown, fox} and {the, quick, red, fox} share three of five distinct words → 3/5 = 0.6. Cell 1: {alpha, beta, gamma} and {beta, gamma, delta} share two of four → 0.5.

Example 2: Identical And Disjoint¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"same words here"})
                 .jaccard_tokens(pluss::make_note({"same words here"}))
          << "\n";
std::cout << pluss::make_note({"a b c"}).jaccard_tokens(pluss::make_note({"d e f"}))
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["1.0"]
Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["0.0"]

Example 3: Empty Sets¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({""}).jaccard_tokens(pluss::make_note({""})) << "\n";
std::cout << pluss::make_note({"a b"}).jaccard_tokens(pluss::make_note({""})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["1.0"]
Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["0.0"]

Two empty word sets score 1.0; one empty against one non-empty scores 0.0.

Example 4: Scalar Broadcast¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"cat dog", "dog bird fish"})
        .jaccard_tokens(pluss::make_note({"dog"})))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["0.5", "0.333333"]

The single right-hand cell {dog} is scored against each left-hand cell: {cat, dog} → 1/2; {dog, bird, fish} → 1/3.

Example 5: Shape Is Preserved¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({{"cat dog", "sun moon"}, {"red blue", "up down"}})
        .jaccard_tokens(pluss::make_note({{"cat fish", "sun moon"}, {"red green", "left right"}})))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["0.333333", "1.0"], 
  ["0.333333", "0.0"]
]

See Also¶

  • Note::overlap_tokens: |A ∩ B| / min(|A|, |B|) — scores containment instead of mutual similarity.

  • Note::intersect_tokens: the shared words, not a score.

  • Note::jaccard_terms: the same score over content words only.
